name: Defining actions in the store
description: Actions are just functions defined alongside state inside the create() callback, closing over set (and optionally get) to update the store.
notes: Because actions live on the same object as state, they are automatically available wherever the store hook is used — no dispatch or action types required.

name: Calling actions from components
description: Components select an action from the store using the hook, the same way they select state, and call it directly like a normal function.
notes: Action references are stable across renders, so selecting them doesn't cause unnecessary re-renders.

name: Actions updating state via set()
description: Actions update the store exclusively by calling set() with a partial state or an updater function — there is no separate reducer/dispatch step like in Redux.
notes: Because set() merges shallowly, an action only needs to return the keys it changes.

name: Actions calling other actions
description: Actions can call other actions on the same store via get(), enabling composition without duplicating logic.
notes: Keep composed action chains simple — deeply nested calls can make state changes harder to trace.

name: Actions outside components
description: Because actions are plain functions on the store, they can be invoked outside React (e.g. in event handlers, utilities, or tests) via getState().
example:
// In a non-component utility file
useCounterStore.getState().increment();
notes: This avoids needing to pass actions down as props or through context for non-component code.

name: Grouping actions in an actions object
description: For larger stores, actions are sometimes grouped under a nested actions key (e.g. state.actions.increment) to visually separate them from data fields.
notes: This is a convention, not a Zustand requirement — it helps when a store has many actions and you want to select 'actions' as a stable group.
